questions.q: What is the main point of the passage?
options: Experts agree that prostate screening should be dropped for most men over fifty
The task force now backs annual rectal exams for all men starting at age forty-five
The cancer society now urges routine blood tests for men 50 to 69, which experts debate
Prostate cancer screening was found to raise deaths in a large European study
questions.explain: The passage reports the A.C.S. reversal toward routine P.S.A. screening and experts' concerns about harms.

questions.q: How often do the new guidelines recommend screening for men ages 50 to 69?
options: Every year
Every five years
Every three years
Every two years
questions.explain: The guidelines recommend a blood test every two years for men 50 to 69.

questions.q: In the European trial after 23 years, how much lower was the risk of prostate cancer death among screened men?
options: 13 percent
40 percent
2.5 percent
65 percent
questions.explain: The risk of death was 13 percent lower among men screened regularly, about two deaths averted per 1,000.

questions.q: According to Dr. Brawley, what is the primary reason Black men have worse outcomes?
options: Their cancers are far more aggressive in biology
They have less access to high quality care
They are diagnosed at a much younger age by law
They are screened less often than white men
questions.explain: Dr. Brawley said the primary reason is less access to high quality care, since outcomes match when care is the same.

questions.q: Why does Dr. Krist doubt the new guidelines will work as hoped?
options: He expects doctors to order the test for everyone by default
He thinks every two years is too infrequent to catch tumors
He believes the European trial data was badly flawed
He fears men will refuse blood tests and skip all follow-up
questions.explain: Krist said most physicians will just get the test on everyone, so harms remain and benefits may not come.
